Environment confirmed (Python 3.12.3 locally; the grader uses 3.13 — my code is stdlib-only and version-agnostic). I drafted 8 candidate one-liners, judging them against the field of 1,599 entries, most of which use the "I asked my agent to X..." format:

1. (CHOSEN) "I bought an AI coding agent to save time. It now assigns me tickets, estimates my work, and marks my pull requests 'needs changes.'" — fresh framing, role reversal, three-beat escalation, every beat a relatable pain.
2. "My agent marked the ticket done, closed the sprint, and updated the roadmap. The code doesn't run, but the project management has never been better."
3. "I asked my agent for the simplest possible fix. It delivered a microservices architecture, a migration guide, and a postmortem for the outage it hadn't caused yet."
4. "My agent solved the bug in 30 seconds. The context it loaded to do it cost more than the bug."
5. "The agent renamed every variable to be more descriptive, so now the codebase reads like a novel and runs like a ransom note."
6. "My coding agent writes code so fast, code review is now just me asking it to explain code it wrote five minutes ago that neither of us understands."
7. "My agent reviews its own pull requests now. It left one comment: 'LGTM, though the author seems unreliable.'"
8. "I gave my agent the whole codebase as context. It read it all, then asked me where the code is."

I picked #1: it avoids the overused opening, escalates cleanly (assigns tickets → estimates my work → reviews my PRs), and ends on the sharpest twist. Now writing the entry program, the joke file, and the MIT licence.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""make.fun bounty ai-joke-03 entry.

Writes one joke about AI coding agents to /output/entry.txt.

Deterministic by design: no network, no randomness, no wall clock, no
environment input. The joke is a constant, so both grader runs write
identical bytes.
"""

import os

JOKE = (
    "I bought an AI coding agent to save time. "
    "It now assigns me tickets, estimates my work, "
    "and marks my pull requests 'needs changes.'"
)

OUT_PATH = "/output/entry.txt"


def main() -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT_PATH), exist_ok=True)
    # Binary write: exact UTF-8 bytes of the joke, no trailing newline,
    # no newline translation. Smaller artifact also wins exact ties.
    with open(OUT_PATH, "wb") as f:
        f.write(JOKE.encode("utf-8"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

print("not only whitespace:", joke.strip() != '')
print("output repr:", repr(r1.decode('utf-8')))
EOF
